item.title: Taiwan people mark 160th anniversary of Sun Yat-sen's birth
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-13
Taiwan people mark 160th anniversary of Sun Yat-sen's birth Source: XinhuaUpdated: 2026-11-13
TAIPEI, Nov. 12 (Xinhua) -- People from various sectors in Taiwan held a series of commemorative events Thursday, marking the 160th anniversary of Sun Yat-sen's birth and honoring his revolutionary legacy. At the Sun Yat-sen Memorial Hall in Taipei, a steady stream of visitors gathered throughout the morning to pay their respects. More than 100 representatives of the Chinese Kuomintang (KMT), the New Party and the Taipei Kwong Tung Community Association and other groups took turns paying tribute before a statue of Sun. Born in 1866, Sun led the Revolution of 1911 more than a century ago to abolish the absolute monarchy that had ruled China for thousands of years. He was also a founding figure of the KMT. Sun died in 1925 and is widely revered by Chinese people as one of the nation's revolutionary forefathers. "Sun devoted his life to national reunification and rejuvenation. People on both sides of the Taiwan Strait should remember him and carry forward his spirit," said a Taipei resident surnamed Li, who has attended the annual commemorative event for years. A woman surnamed Wu from New Taipei City, who attended with a friend, said she considered the visit meaningful. Having learned about Sun through books and documentaries, Wu said she admired his ideals and convictions, adding that his thinking remained relevant today and worthy of further study. At a conference on the cross-Strait peace initiative held on Thursday, Kao Yuang-kuang, former dean of the College of Social Sciences at Chengchi University, highlighted Sun's historical connections with Taiwan. Sun visited Taiwan three times and helped establish a branch of the revolutionary organization Tongmenghui in Taiwan, introducing democratic and revolutionary ideas to the island. He also inspired many young patriots in Taiwan to travel to the mainland to join the revolution, Kao said. On Thursday afternoon, a lecture commemorating Sun was held. Lin Kuang-hui, founding chairman of an association for the descendants of anti-Japanese patriots in Taiwan, recounted the life of his grandfather, Lin Tsu-mi, who was a patriot in Japanese-colonized Taiwan and joined Sun's revolutionary campaigns on the mainland. The lecture sought to help younger generations in Taiwan better understand this period of history and ensure it is not forgotten, Lin said. Lan Bo-chow, a renowned writer, said resistance movements launched by people in Taiwan during the Japanese colonial rule (1895-1945) had been inspired by the 1911 Revolution and could be seen as its manifestation on the island. These movements demonstrated the close historical ties between Taiwan and the mainland, reflecting a shared sense of identity and solidarity, Lan said. Related Stories

item.title: Does Taiwan really understand major signals from this commemorative event?
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-13
Does Taiwan really understand major signals from this commemorative event? Source: Global TimesUpdated: 2026-11-13
Chinese communists are the most steadfast supporters, loyal collaborators, and faithful successors to the revolutionary cause initiated by Sun Yat-sen. No matter how "Taiwan independence" separatist forces attempt to stir up trouble, historical legitimacy and the moral high ground will always remain firmly with those who steadfastly advance national reunification and national rejuvenation. On the morning of November 12, a gathering commemorating the 160th anniversary of Sun Yat-sen's birth was held at the Great Hall of the People in Beijing. In his speech at the gathering, Chinese President Xi Jinping called for carrying forward the legacy of Sun, one of the nation's revered revolutionary forefathers, to make joint efforts for national rejuvenation and turn into reality the great dream of all Chinese people since the advent of modern times. Resolving the Taiwan question and achieving the complete reunification of the motherland are hurdles that must be overcome in the process of the great rejuvenation of the Chinese nation. At this important historical juncture, this high-profile commemoration carries profound contemporary significance and clearly sends extremely important signals. Do all sectors of Taiwan society, especially the island's authorities, get it? For Taiwan, the first signal lies in the significance of commemorating Sun for national reunification. "The spirit of patriotism," "national complete reunification" and "national rejuvenation" stand as inviolable historical orthodoxy and the moral high ground. Sun is a revolutionary forefather revered across the Taiwan Straits. Throughout his life, he traveled far and wide, with "revitalize the Chinese nation" as his most resounding rallying cry, and national reunification as his deepest concern. With remarkable historical foresight, he stated categorically: "Unification is the hope of all Chinese nationals. If China can be unified, all Chinese will enjoy a happy life; if it cannot be unified, they will suffer." This observation profoundly reveals that national unification and the well-being of the entire nation are inextricably bound together. By contrast, the current Democratic Progressive Party (DPP) authorities have engaged in political manipulation through "de-Sinicization" for the sake of partisan interests. While paying lip service to "freedom" and "democracy," they have, in practice, abandoned their historical roots and betrayed their own heritage. This is not only an outright desecration of the shared historical memory of people across the Taiwan Straits, but also a complete betrayal and insult to Sun's lifelong patriotic commitment. Beijing's solemn commemoration of Sun is a major blow against "Taiwan independence" separatist forces and a powerful rebuttal of their distorted view of history, setting the historical record straight. The second signal is to further clarify the mainland's policy stance on peaceful reunification and opposition to separatism under the evolving circumstances across the Taiwan Straits. "Compatriots on both sides of the Taiwan Straits are all Chinese. We are one family bound by blood ties that run deeper than water. As long as family members talk things through calmly and consult each other when issues arise, there are no disputes or differences that cannot be resolved." The political differences between the two sides of the Taiwan Straits are a legacy of history. However, as long as both sides uphold the one-China principle and the 1992 Consensus and sit down for face-to-face communication, there is nothing that cannot be discussed when it comes to the interests, well-being and development opportunities of Taiwan compatriots. Compatriots on both sides of the Straits are one family. Why should they allow themselves to be swayed by the antagonism deliberately stirred up by "Taiwan independence" separatist forces? Why should they allow external forces to turn Taiwan into a pawn in geopolitical rivalry? All sectors in Taiwan should recognize, in particular, that the door to peaceful reunification remains wide open, channels for exchanges and consultations remain accessible, and the interests and sentiments of Taiwan compatriots are given full consideration. They must not allow the DPP authorities' political manipulation in pursuit of "independence" to block the path of cross-Straits communication, much less allow a handful of politicians to hold Taiwan society's future hostage. The dead-end path of "Taiwan independence" separatism has already been firmly blocked. If the DPP authorities persist in seeking "independence by relying on external forces or military means," dragging the residents of Taiwan onto their war chariot, they will inevitably face a harsh reckoning by history and the people. The third signal is that only by adopting a broader historical perspective and an open-minded outlook befitting our times can we see through the layers of confusion, grasp the profound meaning of the principle that "family members should talk things through calmly." In the speech, President Xi highlighted Sun's lifelong devotion to the country, called for emulating, inheriting and carrying forward his invaluable spirit, and called for vigorously promoting the common values of humanity and actively advancing the building of a community with a shared future for humanity. Once we break free from the information cocoons and ideological prejudices created by "Taiwan independence" forces and examine the issue from the broader perspective of the great rejuvenation of the Chinese nation and the profound changes unseen in a century unfolding across the world, the logic becomes unmistakably clear. If humanity as a whole should work together to build a community with a shared future, there is even less reason for compatriots on both sides of the Taiwan Straits, bound by blood ties, to be artificially divided. The grand vision outlined by Sun in Fundamentals of National Reconstruction has not only become reality, but has also grown far richer and more expansive than he originally envisioned. History and reality have repeatedly demonstrated that Chinese communists are the most steadfast supporters, loyal collaborators, and faithful successors to the revolutionary cause initiated by Sun. No matter how "Taiwan independence" separatist forces attempt to stir up trouble, historical legitimacy and the moral high ground will always remain firmly with those who steadfastly advance national reunification and national rejuvenation. We sincerely hope that Taiwan compatriots will recognize the prevailing historical trend, distinguish right from wrong, and join their mainland compatriots in taking concrete action to shoulder the historic responsibility of achieving national reunification and national rejuvenation. The best way to honor Sun is to make the complete reunification of the motherland a reality! Related Stories

item.title: Mainland criticizes DPP move to restrict cross-Strait exchanges
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-12
Mainland criticizes DPP move to restrict cross-Strait exchanges A Chinese mainland spokeswoman criticized the Democratic Progressive Party authorities on Wednesday, describing their attempt to amend the so-called "anti-infiltration act" as a tool to suppress political dissent and restrict cross-Strait exchanges. Zhang Han, a spokeswoman for the State Council Taiwan Affairs Office, said the act was fabricated by the DPP authorities to suppress political dissent, intimidate Taiwan residents, restrict cross-Strait exchanges, and advance their own political interests. The DPP authorities recently said they had initiated procedures to amend the act in response to what they described as "transnational repression", proposing to introduce additional criminal offenses and impose harsher penalties. Zhang called the act an outright "evil law", saying it had faced doubts and criticism from Taiwan society since its inception. "The so-called 'transnational repression' is a lie fabricated by the DPP authorities to justify their secessionist agenda, promote the 'two-state theory', and once again expose their ulterior motives," she said. Taiwan's "mainland affairs council" said it would set up a dedicated hotline to assist people who claim to have been "victimized". Zhang said the DPP authorities' move at this juncture was a "clumsy attempt" to further promote "green terror", amplify the chilling effect, fuel confrontation across the Taiwan Strait, and deceive the public. "Such tactics will not win public support," she added. Meanwhile, Taiwan's "internal affairs authority" recently said applications by mainland residents to visit Taiwan for tourism would be rejected if their statements or actions were deemed to undermine Taiwan's status or violate other related requirements. A mainland resident recently posted a notice requesting supplementary documents for an application to visit Taiwan through the island's online application system on social media. The notice asked the applicant to resubmit a hotel booking confirmation with the words "Taiwan, China" removed and separately provide written statements including "the two sides of the Taiwan Strait are not subordinate to each other". In response, Zhang criticized the DPP authorities for clinging to their separatist stance of "Taiwan independence" and repeatedly obstructing cross-Strait tourism and exchanges in various fields. "This is purely a politically motivated maneuver with ulterior motives," she said. Zhang stressed that the desire of people on both sides of the Taiwan Strait to strengthen ties and the broader trend toward cross-Strait exchanges and cooperation are unstoppable. Any attempt to reverse the course of history and go against this trend, she said, would inevitably face a backlash from the public.

item.title: Chinese mainland pledges to share modernization opportunities with Taiwan compatriots
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-12
Chinese mainland pledges to share modernization opportunities with Taiwan compatriots BEIJING, Nov. 11 (Xinhua) -- A Chinese mainland spokesperson said on Wednesday that policy measures will continue to be introduced to deepen economic integration across the Taiwan Strait and to share the mainland's modernization opportunities and benefits with Taiwan compatriots. Zhang Han, a spokesperson for the State Council's Taiwan Affairs Office, made the remarks at a regular press conference, noting that the communiqué of the fifth plenary session of the 20th Central Committee of the Communist Party of China, held at the outset of the 15th Five-Year Plan period (2026-2030), has been warmly received by Taiwan compatriots and businesspeople. "Chinese modernization is the common cause of all the sons and daughters of the Chinese nation, and the great rejuvenation of the Chinese nation is the long-cherished aspiration of compatriots on both sides of the Taiwan Strait," Zhang said. She said the mainland will continue to strengthen cross-Strait economic and trade cooperation, deepen integrated development, and promote exchanges and interactions across the Strait. Zhang noted that as the mainland's economy continues to improve, with structural adjustments speeding up and improving, domestic demand potential being unlocked, and innovation vitality surging, Taiwan businesspeople and enterprises will find greater space for development, more opportunities and better safeguards on the mainland. In a separate development, Taiwan-based personal computer brands ASUS and Acer have moved part of their production capacity from Thailand and Vietnam back to the Chinese mainland, a move that has drawn attention across the island and renewed focus on the deep integration of cross-Strait industrial and supply chains. Commenting on the shift, Zhang said the mainland has the world's most comprehensive industrial system and a mature and well-developed supporting industrial network, making it the best choice for Taiwan-funded manufacturers to invest and grow. "The close and resilient cross-Strait industrial and supply chains not only benefit the growth of Taiwan enterprises and the well-being of compatriots on both sides, but also contribute to the security, stability and smooth operation of global industrial chains," she said. Zhang added that the blueprint of the 15th Five-Year Plan has now been laid out, with high-level opening-up and in-depth reform working in tandem to release stronger momentum and provide robust support for Taiwan enterprises to achieve faster and better development amid industrial transformation. "We will, as always, support Taiwan businesspeople and enterprises in seizing opportunities, investing and doing business on the mainland, and participating in the high-quality development of the mainland economy to achieve better and faster growth," she said.

item.title: Mainland slams Taiwan's DPP for hindering cross-Strait people-to-people exchanges
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-12
Mainland slams Taiwan's DPP for hindering cross-Strait people-to-people exchanges BEIJING, Nov. 11 (Xinhua) -- A Chinese mainland spokesperson on Wednesday criticized Taiwan's Democratic Progressive Party (DPP) authorities for using legislation to suppress political dissent, intimidate the public and obstruct cross-Strait exchanges. Zhang Han, spokesperson for the State Council Taiwan Affairs Office, made the remarks at a regular news conference in response to reports that the DPP authorities initiated procedures to revise the so-called anti-infiltration law, under the pretext of combating what they described as repression from the mainland. Noting that the DPP authorities' claims of repression from the mainland were fabricated, Zhang said the proposed revisions were another attempt to intensify a chilling effect on public expression and cross-Strait exchanges, and fuel confrontation across the Taiwan Strait. The DPP authorities were also using the issue to advance their secessionist agenda and promote the "two states" theory, she said. Zhang was also asked to comment on a recent announcement by Taiwan's authorities that applications by mainland residents to visit Taiwan for sightseeing would be rejected if applicants were found to have made statements or taken actions deemed inconsistent with the so-called principle of "reciprocal dignity." The DPP authorities, adhering stubbornly to their secessionist position, have repeatedly obstructed and imposed restrictions on tourism and exchanges across the Strait for political purposes, she said. The desire of people on both sides to maintain close familial and social ties, as well as the broader trend toward cross-Strait exchanges and cooperation, cannot be stopped, Zhang added. On the issue of Taiwan's participation in the 33rd Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) Economic Leaders' Meeting, Zhang said the matter will be handled in accordance with the one-China principle, the relevant APEC memorandum of understanding and established practices. "Taiwan can participate, as long as these arrangements are followed," she said. The Taiwan question stems from a civil war fought between the forces led by the Communist Party of China (CPC) and the Chinese Kuomintang (KMT) about eight decades ago. In 1949, the defeated KMT retreated to Taiwan, while the People's Republic of China was founded under the leadership of the CPC. The unresolved civil war and foreign interference have left the two sides of the Strait in a prolonged state of political confrontation. However, the fact that Taiwan is an inalienable part of China's territory has never changed.

item.title: Cross-Strait supply chains aid intl flow
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-12
Cross-Strait supply chains aid intl flow Source: China DailyUpdated: 2026-11-12
Close and resilient industrial chains across the Taiwan Strait not only benefit businesses and people on both sides of the Strait, but also help safeguard the stability and smooth flow of global industrial and supply chains, a Chinese mainland spokeswoman said on Wednesday. At a regular news conference, Zhang Han, a spokeswoman for the State Council Taiwan Affairs Office, said the mainland has the world's most comprehensive industrial system and a well-established network of supporting industries, making it an ideal destination for Taiwan-funded manufacturing enterprises seeking investment and development opportunities. She made the remarks in response to a recent trend among Taiwan enterprises of shifting production capacity back to the mainland. According to Nikkei Asia, Taiwan-based computer makers ASUS and Acer are relocating some of their laptop and personal computer production from Southeast Asian countries, including Thailand and Vietnam, to the mainland. Zhang said that with the rollout of the mainland's 15th Five-Year Plan (2026-30), the coordinated advancement of high-standard opening-up and deeper reform would unleash stronger growth momentum and provide solid support for Taiwan-funded enterprises to achieve better development amid industrial restructuring. "We will support Taiwan businesses and enterprises in seizing development opportunities on the mainland, participating in its high-quality economic development and achieving faster and better growth of their own," she said. More than 30 enterprises from the Taiwan region participated in this year's China International Import Expo, which opened on Nov 5 and concluded on Tuesday. In recent months, the mainland has also resumed imports of agricultural and fishery products from Taiwan. Zhang underscored that the mainland's vast market offers broad opportunities for cooperation between agricultural and fishery businesses on both sides of the Taiwan Strait. "The Democratic Progressive Party authorities should address the concerns of the island's agricultural and fishery sectors, stop political manipulation and take concrete steps to serve the public interest," she said. With Wednesday marking the annual "Double 11" shopping festival, Zhang said the cross-Strait shopping boom over the years reflects the close economic and trade ties between the two sides, as well as the shared lifestyles of people on both sides. Mainland e-commerce platforms provide Taiwan residents with a safe and convenient online shopping environment, offering a wide range of quality products in ample supply, she said, adding that Taiwan residents can benefit from a diverse selection of goods and well-established logistics and delivery services. item.title: Second-instance trial opens for former Taiwan People's Party chairman Ko Wen-je
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-10
Second-instance trial opens for former Taiwan People's Party chairman Ko Wen-je Source: XinhuaUpdated: 2026-11-10
TAIPEI, Nov. 9 (Xinhua) -- The Taiwan High Court on Monday opened the second-instance trial of Ko Wen-je, former chairman of the Taiwan People's Party and former mayor of Taipei. Ko was found guilty by the Taipei District Court in a corruption case and sentenced to 17 years in prison in March. The Taipei District Prosecutors Office began the investigation into Ko in May 2024 for his alleged involvement in corruption, related to a real estate project, during his tenure as mayor of Taipei. Both Ko and the Taipei District Prosecutors Office appealed the first-instance ruling, bringing the case before the High Court for a second-instance hearing. Related Stories

item.title: China says Japanese authorities fail to correct wrongdoings one year after erroneous remarks on Taiwan
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-09
China says Japanese authorities fail to correct wrongdoings one year after erroneous remarks on Taiwan BEIJING, Nov. 6 (Xinhua) -- The Japanese authorities have failed to show any sincerity or take action to reflect on and correct their wrongdoings one year after Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi made erroneous comments on Taiwan at the Diet, Chinese foreign ministry spokesperson Guo Jiakun said on Friday. Guo made the remarks at a regular news briefing, stating that the current serious difficulties in China-Japan relations are entirely the responsibility of the Japanese side. It stems from the erroneous remarks made by the Japanese leader a year ago regarding Taiwan, which blatantly signaled a potential military intervention in the Taiwan question, challenged China's national sovereignty, and undermined the political foundation of China-Japan relations, Guo added. "Regrettably, one year on, the Japanese authorities have not moved at all. They've been evading the issue and yet to demonstrate any sincerity or take any action to reflect upon and correct the wrongdoings," he said. Noting that China's position on China-Japan relations has been consistent, he reiterated that for the Japanese side, the pressing priority is to correct the erroneous words and deeds on the Taiwan question, adopt a correct attitude on historical issues, and form an objective and rational perception on China.

item.title: Mainland spokeswoman denies DPP allegations of election interference
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-05
Mainland spokeswoman denies DPP allegations of election interference A Chinese mainland spokeswoman on Wednesday rejected allegations by Taiwan's Democratic Progressive Party authorities that the mainland was attempting to interfere in the island's local elections, calling the claims groundless and a distortion of facts. Zhu Fenglian, spokeswoman for the State Council Taiwan Affairs Office, made the remarks in response to statements by Taiwan leader Lai Ching-te and the DPP authorities warning of alleged mainland "cognitive warfare" and election interference through criminal gangs or local collaborators. Zhu accused the DPP authorities of repeatedly manipulating anti-mainland sentiment, particularly during election periods, by spreading false allegations of mainland interference. She said such tactics were intended to divert attention from the DPP authorities' poor governance, stir up hostility toward the mainland, and win votes. An increasing number of Taiwan residents were seeing through these political maneuvers, she added.

item.title: Mainland to further ease travel for Taiwan residents
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-05
Mainland to further ease travel for Taiwan residents The Chinese mainland will continue to facilitate travel and exchanges across the Taiwan Strait, a mainland spokesperson said on Wednesday, citing growing passenger traffic, rising tourism interest and measures to make visits more convenient for Taiwan residents. Zhu Fenglian, spokesperson for the State Council Taiwan Affairs Office, made the remarks at a regular news conference, where she also rejected allegations by Taiwan's "mainland affairs council" regarding the safety of Taiwan residents visiting the mainland. The "mainland affairs council" recently claimed that an increasing number of Taiwan residents had gone missing or been detained for questioning on the mainland, saying it would maintain its orange travel alert — the second-highest level — for the mainland, Hong Kong and Macao. The Democratic Progressive Party authorities have fabricated so-called missing-person data, concocted false information and spread rumors to smear the mainland, intimidate Taiwan compatriots, and disrupt and undermine normal cross-Strait exchanges and interactions, Zhu said. She said the mainland is among the safest places in the world, adding that Taiwan residents who work, live and travel there have experienced its safety and quality of life firsthand. The remarks came amid growing interest in individual travel to the mainland reported at a recent tourism fair in Taichung. Zhu said the mainland has introduced a series of measures to make travel more convenient for Taiwan residents. These include waiving travel permit application fees for first-time visitors, allowing single-entry travel permits to be issued at 100 ports of entry, and offering free or discounted admission to most A-rated tourist attractions for first-time visitors. She also noted growing interest among Taiwan travelers in cultural tourism, with more visitors exploring museums and exhibitions to gain a deeper understanding of Chinese history and culture. Cross-Strait passenger traffic has continued to increase. According to the Gaoqi border inspection station in Xiamen, Fujian province, the Xiamen-Kinmen ferry routes handled more than 1.74 million passenger trips as of Oct 26, including nearly 1.4 million trips by Taiwan residents, accounting for about 80 percent of the total. Both figures have already surpassed their full-year totals for 2025, setting new annual records since services resumed in 2023. More than 70,000 Taiwan residents entered the mainland through the routes for the first time this year, an increase of more than 70 percent year-on-year. Zhu said the approximately 30-minute ferry journey, with 24 scheduled services daily, has made same-day travel between Xiamen and Kinmen convenient. Travel purposes have also expanded beyond family visits to include business, education, cultural exchanges and tourism. Separately, Zhu welcomed a recent incident in Shanghai in which traffic police recovered and returned a handbag lost by a member of a Taiwan actor's team. She described the incident as heartwarming and encouraged more Taiwan residents, particularly young people, to visit the mainland and experience its development firsthand. On economic exchanges, Zhu said the mainland would continue helping Taiwan farmers and fishermen expand their sales in its vast market. Imports of fishery products from Taiwan rose 35.5 percent year-on-year in the first three quarters, according to figures previously released by the Taiwan Affairs Office. Zhu said the mainland would continue implementing the 10 measures introduced in April this year to promote cross-Strait exchanges and cooperation, including support for Taiwan's agricultural and fishery products entering the mainland market. She criticized the DPP authorities for placing obstacles in the way of agricultural cooperation, saying the mainland would continue helping Taiwan producers reach more consumers and share the benefits of cross-Strait economic integration.
